scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 constituents — Tech Mahindra, Titan Company, Trent, UltraTech Cement, Wipro (batch 9 of the holders fleet) — read directly from each company's own latest SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b) quarterly shareholding-pattern filing (Tech Mahindra and Wipro at Q4/Q1 FY26-27 i.e. 31.03.2026 and 30.06.2026; Titan at 30.06.2026; Trent at 31.03.2026; UltraTech's most recent PDF actually reachable on its own site was 31.03.2025, so that is used and flagged as older than the others). For each company this records: every individually-named foreign institutional/portfolio holder crossing 1% in Table III (there were only two across all five companies — Government of Singapore in UltraTech and Amansa Holdings Private Limited, a Mauritius-registered FPI vehicle, in Trent); the mandatory BlackRock/Vanguard/NBIM/GIC/Capital Group/Fidelity/Kuwait Investment Authority/ADIA comparison set, tested against all five and absent as a named ≥1% line in every one; LIC of India as the domestic control, present and named directly in four of five (Tech Mahindra 11.44%, Trent 2.9214%, UltraTech 2.45%, and — via an LIC-managed fund product rather than LIC's own direct line, the same distinction the prior batch's file drew for Bharti Airtel — Wipro 2.69% through 'LICI Index Plus Flexi Smart Growth Fund'; Titan's insurance-company breakdown was not disclosed by name in the filing pages reached, recorded as a gap); the aggregate FPI Category I + II percentage and quarter date for each company; and Wipro's ADR depositary bank (JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.), recorded as a custodian holding legal title to depositary receipts, not a beneficial owner. Tech Mahindra's and Titan's promoter groups are themselves Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd and Tata Sons Private Limited / Government of Tamil Nadu respectively — wholly domestic — and are noted for context but not claimed as foreign holdings. UltraTech's and Tech Mahindra's promoter groups each include small (each <1%, so below this file's naming threshold) foreign promoter-group vehicles (UltraTech: four Indonesian/Thai rayon-manufacturing subsidiaries and a Singapore holding company via the historic Aditya Birla Group rayon JV; Tech Mahindra: Mahindra Investment Company Mauritius Limited, 0.42%) — recorded in company notes, not as individual claims, because none crosses the 1% naming threshold used throughout this fleet. This file does not cover adviser mandates or SEBI/RBI rule-change history (out of scope for this batch) and does not re-litigate the BlackRock/Vanguard narrative already calibrated in research/raw/capital/holders.json — it only adds five more data points to that calibration.

symmetryCheck: The same lens (open the primary SEBI shareholding-pattern filing, list every named foreign holder ≥1%, and name LIC's own line alongside it) produced, across this batch's five companies: for the non-BlackRock mandatory controls, exactly one hit — GIC/Government of Singapore at 1.48% of UltraTech, the smallest of the five companies by promoter concentration and the one with the most fragmented FPI base (836 separate Category I entities). BlackRock, Vanguard, NBIM, Capital Group, Fidelity, KIA and ADIA all came back empty in all five, the same result the lens produced on this fleet's first five-company sample (research/raw/capital/holders.json) — two independent samples, ten companies total, and BlackRock/Vanguard have now been individually named ≥1% in zero of them. For LIC, the lens found a directly-named ≥1% line in three of five (Tech Mahindra 11.44%, Trent 2.92%, UltraTech 2.45%) and an LIC-managed fund product (not LIC's own direct line) in a fourth (Wipro 2.69%) — LIC is a more consistently visible, more consistently ≥1%, and on average far larger single named holder across this batch than every mandatory foreign control combined. The one foreign holder that did cross 1% outside the mandatory set, Amansa Holdings Private Limited in Trent (1.00%), is itself a diversified emerging-markets fund manager, not a strategic industrial stake of the kind found in the fleet's first batch (British American Tobacco 22.91% of ITC, Suzuki Motor Corporation's majority stake in Maruti) — no promoter-level or strategic foreign stake was found in any of this batch's five companies, whose promoter groups (Mahindra & Mahindra, the Premji family, Government of Tamil Nadu/Tata Sons, Tata Sons, and the Aditya Birla Group respectively) are overwhelmingly domestic, with only sub-1% foreign promoter-group vehicles surfacing (Mahindra Investment Company Mauritius 0.42% in Tech Mahindra; five Indonesian/Thai rayon-JV entities totalling 0.93% in UltraTech).
